children: Copper demand remains weaker than bullish market sentiment suggests, with the market in a significant surplus and inventories at their highest levels since the start of the century, says Julius Baer analyst Carsten Menke in a note. However, the bank has grown more confident in long-term demand growth thanks to electrification, EVs and data centers. The U.S. accounts for about 6% of global copper consumption but holds around 70% of observable copper inventories, contributing to tightness in other markets, Menke says. Julius Baer upgrades its copper outlook to neutral and raises its three-month and 12-month price targets to $13,250 and $14,500 a metric ton, respectively. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
